title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (988 Colorado Mental Health Line)
summary: Free, confidential, 24/7/365 behavioral health crisis line providing immediate support for anyone experiencing emotional distress, mental health concerns, substance use concerns, or thoughts of suicide.

fields.service summary: Free, confidential, 24/7/365 behavioral health crisis line providing immediate support for anyone experiencing emotional distress, mental health concerns, substance use concerns, or thoughts of suicide.
fields.detailed services: Phone, text, and live chat support; connection to trained specialists; walk-in center referrals; mobile crisis response dispatch; peer support; follow-up care coordination.
fields.population served: Anyone in Colorado experiencing a mental health, substance use, or emotional crisis, regardless of insurance, age, residency, or previous service utilization.
fields.geographic service area: All Colorado.
fields.physical address: N/A — telephone, text, and online service. Walk-in center locations available statewide.
fields.access method: Call 988, text 988, or live chat at 988Colorado.com. Walk-in crisis centers are also available statewide (see Resources 4–7).
fields.eligibility: None — available to anyone in Colorado.
fields.insurance accepted: N/A — no insurance required.
fields.availability for uninsured: Yes — available regardless of insurance status.
fields.languages: Phone and text available in English and Spanish. Live chat available in English and Spanish.
fields.accessibility: TTY users can call 988. Live chat available for those who cannot safely make a phone call.
fields.transportation access: N/A — remote service. Mobile crisis teams can come to the person's location.
fields.restrictions: 988 is for behavioral health crises, not medical emergencies — for medical emergencies, call 911.
fields.important note: As of July 1, 2025, the former Colorado Crisis Services line (1-844-493-8255 / text "TALK" to 38255) routes directly to the 988 Colorado Mental Health Line. The old number still works but connects to the same service. (BHA – 988 Data Dashboard)

title: Mobile Crisis Response (MCR)
summary: A two-person multidisciplinary team that provides face-to-face crisis intervention, screening, assessment, de-escalation, stabilization, safety planning, and coordination with referrals at a person's community- based location.

fields.organization name: Colorado Crisis Services / Behavioral Health Administration
fields.service summary: A two-person multidisciplinary team that provides face-to-face crisis intervention, screening, assessment, de-escalation, stabilization, safety planning, and coordination with referrals at a person's community- based location.
fields.detailed services: Community-based crisis intervention; screening and assessment; de-escalation and stabilization; safety planning; coordination with and referrals to health, social, and other services; follow-up care; transportation arrangement to a facility if needed. MCR teams do not include law enforcement.
fields.population served: All people in Colorado experiencing a self-defined behavioral health crisis, regardless of insurance status, age, residency, or previous service utilization.
fields.geographic service area: Statewide — available through a regional network of mobile crisis providers.
fields.physical address: N/A — team responds to the individual's location in the community.
fields.primary phone number: 988 (dispatched through the 988 Colorado Mental Health Line)
fields.access method: Call or text 988, or live chat at 988Colorado.com. The 988 Colorado team determines the appropriate intervention and dispatches MCR if needed.
fields.eligibility: Available to all people in Colorado in crisis, regardless of insurance status, age, residency, or previous service utilization.
fields.fees: Free for the individual. MCR is a Medicaid-covered benefit; services are provided to all regardless of ability to pay.
fields.insurance accepted: N/A — services available regardless of insurance status.
fields.availability for uninsured: Yes — available regardless of insurance status.
fields.languages: Not confirmed — contact provider. The 988 line offers English and Spanish.
fields.accessibility: Teams respond to the individual's location, including homes and community settings. Telehealth may be used as a component.
fields.transportation access: N/A — team comes to the individual. May arrange transportation to a facility if needed.
fields.response times: Urban areas: within 1 hour of dispatch request. Rural and frontier areas: within 2 hours.
fields.restrictions: MCR is not a replacement for ongoing behavioral health services. MCR cannot be provided in institutions or facilities. MCR teams are not law enforcement.

title: OneHome Coordinated Entry System (Metro Denver Homeless Initiative)
summary: The Coordinated Entry System for the seven-county Metro Denver region that assesses, prioritizes, and matches individuals, youth, and families experiencing homelessness to available housing resources.

fields.service summary: The Coordinated Entry System for the seven-county Metro Denver region that assesses, prioritizes, and matches individuals, youth, and families experiencing homelessness to available housing resources.
fields.detailed services: Standardized assessment of housing needs; prioritization based on vulnerability; matching to housing resources including permanent supportive housing, rapid rehousing, and transitional housing; client choice in housing selection; case conferencing; data management through HMIS.
fields.population served: Individuals (age 25+ with no minor children), families (age 18+ with at least one minor or dependent), veterans (age 18+), and young adults (ages 18–24 with no minor children) experiencing homelessness.
fields.geographic service area: Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, and Jefferson counties. (Clear Creek County is NOT in the OneHome system.)
fields.physical address: N/A — accessed through Access Points and Assessing Partners throughout the seven-county region.
fields.primary phone number: 2-1-1 (for shelter information and referrals); contact specific Access Points directly.
fields.email: contact@onehomeco.org (for case conferencing invitations); HMIShelp@mdhi.org (for HMIS/data questions)
fields.official website: MDHI – Need Help; MDHI – Coordinated Entry
fields.access method: Contact an Access Point (any location where households experiencing homelessness can access the OneHome system and be assessed) or an Assessing Partner (agencies with eligibility criteria for taking assessments). Metro Denver uses a "no wrong door" approach — a household can access coordinated entry at various locations across the seven-county region and is not limited to access points in their county. Street Outreach is also an access point.
fields.eligibility: Must meet HUD's literal homeless criteria: (1) living outside or in a place not meant for human habitation (encampment, car, abandoned building, RV without utilities); (2) living in a shelter, transitional housing, or motel paid for by an agency; (3) exiting an institution (jail, hospital, treatment, rehab) where resided up to 90 days and was in a shelter or place not meant for human habitation immediately before; (4) young adults ages 18–24 at imminent risk of homelessness (will lose housing within 14 days, nowhere to go, no other resources).
fields.accessibility: Access Points may differ by accessibility features — contact specific Access Point.
fields.transportation access: Varies by Access Point location.
fields.restrictions: Clear Creek County is not served by OneHome. Veterans must first verify eligibility by calling the VA at 877- 222-8387 or going to an in-person Access Point.

title: St. Francis Center — Day Center Services (Denver)

fields.resource category: Homelessness and coordinated entry; day shelters; mail/storage; hygiene
fields.service summary: Daytime drop-in center providing showers, phones, mail service, storage, clothing, meals, notary, cell phone charging, social services, wellness services, and housing navigation for men and women experiencing homelessness in metro Denver.
fields.detailed services: Showers (soap, shampoo, towels provided); phones for local calls and message-taking (held 7 days); mail service (anyone may receive mail; government-issued photo ID required for pickup; mail held 7 days); storage for 550 people (30-gallon bag limit; renewed every 30 days; first-come, first-served); clothing room (access in exchange for cleaning chore); cell phone charging (checked in/out); notary services (photo ID required); social services (one-on-one meetings, orientation to shelter/food/clothing, bus fare for medical appointments, ID and Social Security card assistance, housing applications, move-in assistance, family reunification); wellness services (mental health and substance abuse counseling, crisis intervention, referrals, peer recovery specialists, ear acupuncture/acuDetox, hepatitis C testing); on-site partners (Denver Human Services, VA, Denver Health Public Health, Well Power).
fields.population served: Men and women experiencing homelessness. Approximately 600 guests per day on average.
fields.geographic service area: Metro Denver.
fields.physical address: 2323 Curtis Street, Denver, CO 80205 (service-delivery address; public)
fields.hours of operation: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 7:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.; Wednesday: 7:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. (closes at 12:00 p.m. on the 3rd Wednesday of every month for staff meetings); Saturday–Sunday: 7:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m. Closed all day twice annually for staff retreats.
fields.off-site storage hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 8:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. (closed for break 10:00–10:25 a.m.; closed for lunch 11:45 a.m. – 12:30 p.m.); Wednesday: 8:00 a.m. – 12:45 p.m.; 3rd Wednesday: 8:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. No weekend storage access.
fields.access method: Walk-in. No appointment or intake appointment required for general Day Center services.
fields.eligibility: No specific eligibility requirements stated for Day Center services. Anyone may receive mail. Government- issued photo ID required for mail pickup and notary services.
fields.required documents: Government-issued photo ID for mail pickup and notary services. No ID required for general day center access.
fields.fees: Not stated for most services. Hepatitis C testing is free.
fields.accessibility: TTY/TDD available: (800) 659-2656. Additional accessibility not stated — contact provider.
fields.transportation access: RTD serves the Curtis Street area in downtown Denver.
fields.restrictions: Not an overnight shelter — daytime services only. Storage limited to one location per person. Storage limited to 30-gallon bag. Clothing room access requires performing a cleaning chore.

title: Denver CARES — Withdrawal Management and Residential Treatment
summary: 100-bed non-medical, clinically managed treatment facility providing 24/7 withdrawal management (detox) and 45–90 day residential treatment for individuals with substance use disorders, serving the City and County of Denver for nearly five decades.

fields.resource category: Substance use treatment; withdrawal management/detox; residential treatment
fields.organization name: Denver Community Addiction Rehabilitation and Evaluation Services (Denver CARES), operated by Denver Health
fields.program name: Denver CARES Withdrawal Management and Residential Treatment
fields.service summary: 100-bed non-medical, clinically managed treatment facility providing 24/7 withdrawal management (detox) and 45–90 day residential treatment for individuals with substance use disorders, serving the City and County of Denver for nearly five decades.
fields.detailed services: Withdrawal management (detox): safe and humane withdrawal from alcohol and/or drugs; RN triage before admission; vital-sign checks; sleeping accommodations; medication management pathways for alcohol, opioid, and methamphetamine use disorders; MAT if applicable; group counseling; well-balanced meals; initial education; harm-reduction education; addiction and recovery counseling; treatment referrals. title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) (Statewide)
summary: Federal nutrition program providing monthly benefits to help low-income households purchase food. Benefits are issued on an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card (also called the Colorado Quest Card), which works like a debit card at authorized food stores.

fields.service summary: Federal nutrition program providing monthly benefits to help low-income households purchase food. Benefits are issued on an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card (also called the Colorado Quest Card), which works like a debit card at authorized food stores.
fields.detailed services: Monthly food benefits via EBT/Quest Card; Double Up Food Bucks program (doubles SNAP value at participating vendors); museum and cultural center admission discounts with EBT card; EBT card can be used at any authorized store nationwide displaying the EBT or Quest card logo.
fields.population served: Low-income households. May qualify if: making low wages; income below 200% FPL; unemployed or working part-time; receiving other assistance (Colorado Works, SSI); children; students; adults 18–56 with no children in the home (ABAWDs).
fields.geographic service area: Statewide.
fields.county or counties served: All Colorado counties. Each county's human services department determines eligibility and authorizes benefits.
fields.access method: Apply online through Colorado PEAK; use MyCOBenefits mobile app (iOS/Android); submit paper application (English, Spanish, large-print) by mail, fax, or in person to county human services office. Application assistance: call Hunger Free Colorado at (855) 855-4626.
fields.eligibility: Based on income, resources, and household size. Income must be below 200% FPL (see table above). ABAWDs (adults 18–56 without dependents) must work or participate in approved work activities at least 80 hours/month.
fields.required documents: Not specified on official page — county may require proof of income, identity, residency, and household composition.
fields.languages: Applications available in English, Spanish, large-print English, and large-print Spanish.
fields.accessibility: Online, mobile app, and paper application options.
fields.restrictions: ABAWD work requirements reinstated following end of federal Public Health Emergency. Federal changes effective October 1, 2023, expanded work requirements to ages 50–54.

title: Colorado Works / Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) (Statewide)
summary: Colorado's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program, providing monthly cash assistance to families with children for basic needs including food, housing, and clothing. Also provides employment support, training, education, and case management.

fields.service summary: Colorado's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program, providing monthly cash assistance to families with children for basic needs including food, housing, and clothing. Also provides employment support, training, education, and case management.
fields.detailed services: Monthly cash payment (via EBT card or direct deposit); schooling; training; job assistance; help setting goals; help building community connections; case management; childcare assistance; child support services. When applying for Colorado Works, applicants are also applying for food assistance, Medicaid, and child support services.
fields.population served: Families with children.
fields.geographic service area: Statewide.
fields.county or counties served: All Colorado counties. Administered by county human services departments.
fields.official website: CDHS – Colorado Works; Boulder County – Colorado Works
fields.access method: Apply through Colorado PEAK; use MyCOBenefits mobile app; submit paper application; or contact county human services office.
fields.eligibility: Must be pregnant or caring for a child under 18; live in Colorado; be a U.S. citizen, legal alien, refugee, or permanent resident; have family income less than $75,000/year; meet resource limits (bank accounts, vehicles). Must cooperate with child support and participate in work activities.
fields.benefit duration: Up to 60 months (5 years) total over a lifetime.
fields.languages: Applications available in English, Spanish, large-print English, and large-print Spanish.
fields.restrictions: 60-month lifetime limit. Must participate in work activities unless applying for SSI. Must cooperate with child support.

title: Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND) / Aid to the Blind (Statewide)
summary: State financial assistance program providing monthly cash benefits to eligible individuals with disabilities (ages 18–59, or 0–59 for blindness) who are unable to work and are applying for or receiving SSI.

fields.organization name: Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) / County Human Services
fields.program name: Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND) / Aid to the Blind
fields.service summary: State financial assistance program providing monthly cash benefits to eligible individuals with disabilities (ages 18–59, or 0–59 for blindness) who are unable to work and are applying for or receiving SSI.
fields.detailed services: Monthly cash benefit. Two components: AND-State Only (for those not receiving SSI) and AND-Colorado Supplement (for those receiving SSI). Must apply for SSI through Social Security Administration.
fields.population served: Individuals aged 18–59 with disabilities (or 0–59 for blindness) who are unable to do any kind of work for at least 6 months.
fields.geographic service area: Statewide.
fields.county or counties served: All Colorado counties. Administered by county human services departments.
fields.access method: Apply online at Colorado PEAK; call Hunger Free Colorado at (855) 855-4626; or submit paper application to county human services office by mail, drop-off, fax, or email. Aer applying, applicant will be contacted for a required interview.
fields.eligibility: Age 18–59 (AND-State Only) or 0–59 (blindness/Colorado Supplement); U.S. citizen, naturalized citizen, or eligible legal resident; Colorado resident; must apply for SSI at SSA; must be certified by a Colorado- licensed doctor as disabled for at least 6 months and unable to do any kind of work; income cannot exceed $248/month; resources $2,000 or less (individual) or $3,000 or less (married couple).
fields.required documents: Completed application; Authorization for Reimbursement of Interim Assistance form (IM-14); application for SSI through SSA; Med 9 doctor's form (completed by a doctor); verification of income.
fields.benefit delivery: Not confirmed — likely EBT card (same as OAP).
fields.redetermination: Periodic — applicant will be mailed a packet or notified by PEAK.
fields.restrictions: Must apply for SSI. Must have doctor's certification (Med 9). Income limit $248/month is very restrictive.

fields.service summary: Former federal program that provided discounts on broadband service and connected devices for eligible low-income households. The program ended in 2024 due to lack of funding from Congress.
fields.detailed services: No longer accepting applications or enrollments as of February 7, 2024. The program provided up to $30/month off internet service (up to $75/month on Tribal lands) and a one-time device discount of up to $100.
fields.population served: Formerly eligible low-income households.
fields.geographic service area: Nationwide (former).
fields.current status: DISCONTINUED — The program stopped accepting new consumer applications and enrollments on February 7, 2024. April 2024 was the final full month of ACP benefits. The program ended due to lack of additional funding from Congress.

title: Colorado Division of Veterans Affairs (DVA) (Statewide)
summary: State agency providing advocacy and assistance to Colorado veterans, family members, and survivors in securing state and federal veterans benefits through specially trained service officers. DVA is not the Federal VA — it is a state government department.

fields.resource category: Veterans; benefits; claims assistance; state agency
fields.service summary: State agency providing advocacy and assistance to Colorado veterans, family members, and survivors in securing state and federal veterans benefits through specially trained service officers. DVA is not the Federal VA — it is a state government department.
fields.detailed services: Advocacy for veterans, family members, and survivors; assistance throughout the VA claims process for state and federal benefits; appeals of VA decisions; central source of information on veterans benefits, rights, and issues; directs, trains, and assists County Veterans Service Officers (CVSOs) in each county; serves as advocate and attorney-in-fact before the Board of Veteran Affairs.
fields.population served: Colorado veterans, family members, survivors, and eligible dependents.
fields.geographic service area: Statewide.
fields.access method: Make an appointment with your County Veterans Service Officer (CVSO) for assistance with claims and benefits. Stay in contact with your CVSO throughout the claims process. DVA assists claimants throughout the claims process and with appeals.

title: VA National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (National/Statewide)
summary: 24/7 free, confidential hotline connecting homeless or at-risk veterans to their nearest VA for help with housing, healthcare, and supportive services.

fields.program name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
fields.service summary: 24/7 free, confidential hotline connecting homeless or at-risk veterans to their nearest VA for help with housing, healthcare, and supportive services.
fields.detailed services: Connection to local VA homeless programs and services. VA homeless programs include: HUD-VASH (permanent supportive housing); SSVF (homelessness prevention and rapid re-housing); Grant & Per Diem (transitional housing); HCHV (outreach and residential treatment); HVCES (job preparedness); Veterans Justice Programs (outreach and case management for justice-involved veterans); HPACT (primary care for homeless veterans); DCHV (residential rehabilitation and treatment); Legal Services for Veterans; Homeless Veterans Dental Program; Stand Down Events (1–3 day service fairs).
fields.population served: Veterans who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness, including formerly homeless veterans, at- risk veterans, justice-involved veterans, and veterans and their families.
fields.geographic service area: Nationwide.
fields.hours of operation: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
fields.access method: Call (877) 424-3838. Trained professionals connect callers to their nearest VA for help.
fields.eligibility: Veterans who are homeless or at imminent risk of homelessness.
fields.currently active: Yes — VA announced FY2027 grant awards through GPD and SSVF programs.

title: Colorado Child Care Assistance Program (CCCAP)
summary: Child care assistance for low-income families who are homeless, working, searching for work, or in school. Families enrolled in Colorado Works (TANF) can also use CCCAP. Families may choose a licensed child care center, licensed family child care home, or a friend/neighbor/relative caretaker. Colorado Shines child care search tool helps find licensed providers that accept CCCAP.

fields.physical address: Administered through each county's Department of Social/Human Services; state office: Colorado Department of Early Childhood, Division of Early Care and Learning
fields.primary phone number: No state phone number listed — apply through county department of human/social services. ATS Help Desk email: CDEC_ats_helpdesk@state.co.us
fields.services: Child care assistance for low-income families who are homeless, working, searching for work, or in school. Families enrolled in Colorado Works (TANF) can also use CCCAP. Families may choose a licensed child care center, licensed family child care home, or a friend/neighbor/relative caretaker. Colorado Shines child care search tool helps find licensed providers that accept CCCAP.
fields.eligibility: Each county sets its own eligibility. Counties must serve families with income at or below 185% of the federal poverty guideline. Counties will not serve families with income over 85% of state median income. Families may be responsible for a parent fee based on gross income, household size, and number of children in care. As of July 1, 2023, cooperation with Child Support Services is no longer required for CCCAP eligibility.
fields.required documents: Written verification of employment or education program within 30 days of applying. During annual redetermination: signed Redetermination of Eligibility Form, 30 days of paycheck stubs, work schedule. When requesting provider authorization: provider's name and address.
fields.geographic service area: Statewide — administered at county level

title: Rocky Mountain Human Services (RMHS)

summary: Public transportation for people with disabilities. Door-to-door paratransit service. Access-on-Demand is a premium, opt-in, curb-to-curb service available only to Access-a-Ride customers with active certification.

fields.physical address: RTD, c/o Access-a-Ride, 1660 Blake St., Denver, CO 80202
fields.services: Public transportation for people with disabilities. Door-to-door paratransit service. Access-on-Demand is a premium, opt-in, curb-to-curb service available only to Access-a-Ride customers with active certification.
fields.eligibility: Determined by the impact a disability or disabling condition has on one's ability to use bus/rail service — NOT solely by the presence of a disabling condition. Established under Federal guidelines.
fields.access method: Complete Access-a-Ride Certification Application and Medical Verification Form (6 pages total). Return via USPS to 1660 Blake St., Denver, CO 80202, or fax to (303) 299-2169. Must participate in in-person certification appointment. RTD provides transportation to the appointment if needed. Applications not completed within 90 days are withdrawn.
fields.required documents: Completed and signed application form; completed Medical Verification Form (by provider); photo ID card for certification appointment; mobility aids; oxygen for 3+ hours if used; medications for 3+ hours; personal care assistant if needed.

title: Colorado Low-income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP)
summary: Federally funded program providing assistance with a portion of winter home heating costs. Benefit paid directly to primary heating fuel vendor in most cases. Does NOT pay the entire cost of home heating. Heating system repair/replacement available (furnace, wood-burning stove). Does NOT cover portable/temporary heating (electric heaters, portable heaters).

fields.organization name: Colorado Low-income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) — CDHS
fields.services: Federally funded program providing assistance with a portion of winter home heating costs. Benefit paid directly to primary heating fuel vendor in most cases. Does NOT pay the entire cost of home heating. Heating system repair/replacement available (furnace, wood-burning stove). Does NOT cover portable/temporary heating (electric heaters, portable heaters).
fields.operating period: Winter season: November through April. 2025–2026 season: November 1, 2025 – April 30, 2026. Assistance can be received only once each season. Most non-emergency applications processed within 10–25 days. Emergency expedited processing in 10 days for heating emergencies.
fields.eligibility: Must pay home heating costs (directly to utility company or to landlord as part of rent). Maximum household income at or below 60% of state median income. Must provide proof of lawful presence in the United States for self and household members born outside the U.S. Must reside in the dwelling stated on application. If heat included in rent, may qualify if not in subsidized housing and proper documentation provided.
fields.required documents: Proof of lawful presence: Naturalization Certificate, Born Abroad Certificate, U.S. Passport, Permanent Resident Card, or Documentation of Refugee/Asylee status. Income verification. Proof of heating costs.
fields.fees: Free (benefit is a grant, not a loan)
fields.geographic service area: Statewide
